answer: Tie payouts to verifiable useful work, not identity count. Each epoch publishes benchmark tasks with objectively checkable answers, so a receipt only its own distinct computation can produce. A controller minting a hundred clones must compute a hundred separate proofs: one proof cannot be spent twice, and scripts that copy cheaply cannot compute cheaply. Like a ripple across a pond, the farmer's advantage fades against per-puppet cost. Self-defeating either way: jade-grade results enrich the commons no matter which sable mask signs them, so a flooded fleet only donates more work.
